I, {patient}, ID {document}, state that I have been clearly informed by {doctor} about my eye health and about the examinations that will be performed: visual acuity, refraction, tonometry, dilation of the pupils with drops, slit lamp examination, fundus examination and the complementary studies that may be needed.

I understand that the dilating drops may cause blurred vision and sensitivity to light for several hours, so I must not drive afterwards, and that, exceptionally, they may cause an increase of the eye pressure or allergic reactions.

I was able to ask all my questions, I know that I can revoke this consent at any time (Law 26.529) and I authorize {company} to perform these examinations and to keep my clinical record. Date: {date}.

I, {patient}, ID {document}, authorize {doctor} and the surgical team of {company} to perform the following procedure: {procedure}.

I have been informed about the purpose of the procedure, the expected benefits, the alternatives (including not having it done), the type of anesthesia and the most frequent and the most serious risks: infection, bleeding, inflammation, increase of the eye pressure, need of a new surgery and, exceptionally, loss of vision.

I understand that medicine is not an exact science and that no specific result can be guaranteed. I commit to follow the indications and to attend the post-operative controls. I can revoke this consent before the procedure (Law 26.529). Date: {date}.

I, {patient}, ID {document}, have been diagnosed with cataract. The surgery ({procedure}) consists of removing the opaque lens through a small incision by phacoemulsification and replacing it with an intraocular lens whose power is calculated from the biometry.

The aim is to improve my vision, but a specific result is not guaranteed and I may need glasses for distance and / or near after the surgery. The possible risks include: inflammation, increase of the eye pressure, corneal edema, rupture of the posterior capsule with need of a second surgery, macular edema, posterior capsule opacification (treated with laser), retinal detachment and infection inside the eye (endophthalmitis), which can cause severe loss of vision.

The alternative is not to have the surgery and to keep using glasses while they are useful. I commit to use the prescribed drops and to attend the controls on day 1, week 1 and month 1. I can revoke this consent before the surgery (Law 26.529). Date: {date}.

I, {patient}, ID {document}, request the refractive surgery {procedure} to reduce my dependence on glasses or contact lenses. I know that it is an elective procedure and that glasses and contact lenses are valid alternatives.

I have been informed of the possible risks: residual or regressive refractive error that may need a retreatment, dry eye, halos and glare at night, flap complications (LASIK), pain and slower recovery (PRK), corneal haze, infection and, exceptionally, corneal ectasia. Presbyopia is not corrected and will appear with age.

I commit to follow the post-operative indications and controls. I can revoke this consent before the procedure (Law 26.529). Date: {date}.

I, {patient}, ID {document}, authorize the treatment {procedure}: the injection of a medication (anti-VEGF or corticosteroid) inside the eye, under sterile conditions and topical anesthesia, to treat my macular or retinal disease. I understand that several injections are usually needed.

The possible risks include: subconjunctival hemorrhage, eye discomfort, floaters, transient increase of the eye pressure, inflammation, retinal detachment, cataract and infection inside the eye (endophthalmitis). I must consult immediately if I have pain, redness or loss of vision in the following days.

I can revoke this consent before each injection (Law 26.529). Date: {date}.
Informed consent: glaucoma surgery or laser

I, {patient}, ID {document}, have glaucoma, a chronic disease that damages the optic nerve. The procedure {procedure} aims to lower the eye pressure to slow down the damage; it does not recover the vision already lost.

The possible risks include: pressure too low or too high, inflammation, bleeding, cataract, failure of the filtration with need of new procedures or of continuing the drops, infection and, exceptionally, loss of vision. Alternatives are drops and other laser or surgical techniques.

I commit to attend the controls, which are frequent during the first weeks. I can revoke this consent before the procedure (Law 26.529). Date: {date}.
